entries.title: II Chronicles 2:2
segments: Threescore and ten thousand men--three thousand and six hundred; see notes to

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:3
segments: The establishment and support of the worship of God according to his appointment, and the spread of a knowledge of his salvation, is the most honorable and noble work in which the kings of the earth can engage; by it they not only honor God, but promote their own highest good and the good of the people over whom they are placed.

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:6
segments:
Should build him a house; that is, a house that can contain him. 
 
  Save only to burn sacrifice before him; he wishes Hiram to understand that he does not propose to build a house that shall contain God's majesty and glory, according to the notions of the heathen respecting their gods, but only a house that shall serve as a suitable place for his public worship, which the burning of sacrifices and incense here stands to represent. 
 
The more exalted a good man's views of God, and the more abundant his labors and offerings for Him, the more humble will be his views of himself, and the more entire his sense of dependence on the riches of divine grace.

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:8
segments: Algum-trees; these came in the ships that went to Ophir under the joint management of Hiram's and Solomon's servants, so that Hiram had a share in the work of procuring them.
They seem to be mentioned here along with the trees of Lebanon, because they were used in common with them in the work of the temple.

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:10
segments: Not only the mutual exchange of kind offices, but the exchange of the labor and productions of different countries, may be of service to all.

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:13
segments: Of Huram my father's; or, as some propose to render, Huram Abi; Abi, my father, being an honorary title borne by this artificer, whose name was Huram or Hiram,

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:14
segments: Of the daughters of Dan; in
, this man is called "a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali."  Probably his mother was by birth of the tribe of Dan, but had married into the tribe of Naphtali.

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:16
segments: Joppa; the nearest seaport on the Mediterranean, about forty miles west of Jerusalem.

entries.title: II Chronicles 2:17
segments: With a proper division of labor and union of effort, and with the blessing of God on well-directed diligence and perseverance, the most difficult undertakings may in due time be accomplished.
